m1-harness.title: Build the disposable sandbox pair and the two arm trees; prove the one-path difference
m1-harness.imperative: Under a temp directory build: a sandbox main (git init) and a real git worktree of it; two arm directories each holding a COMPLETE scripts/ tree (treatment = this worktree's current scripts/, control = git archive cbd9aee); a per-arm settings file wiring spine_rail.py then gauge_writer_hook.py as PostToolUse commands BY ABSOLUTE PATH into that arm's tree. Prove by recursive diff that the two arm trees differ ONLY in scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py (and its tests). Nothing under C:/Programs/constellation-skills is written.

postconditions.statement: sandbox main + real git worktree exist under temp; arm trees complete (gauge_writer_hook.py can import its spine_rail.py sibling); recursive diff shows only spine_rail.py differing, captured to evidence
postconditions.satisfied_by: Sandbox pair (git init main + real git worktree add) and both arm trees build. Recursive diff -rq of the two COMPLETE scripts/ trees shows exactly ONE differing file: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py (evidence/arm-diff.txt). Preflight drove each arm's hook on a synthetic payload: both exit 0 and write the store, so both arm trees are complete (no silent sibling-import failure). Treatment resolves the WORKTREE spine with path_source=git_worktree -- derived by shelling out to git worktree list, NOT read from anything the harness handed it (no cd, no --worktree, no absolute --file, no env var). Control resolves the MAIN CHECKOUT path. evidence/preflight-arms.json.

constraints: arms differ only in the absolute hook path
never hand-inject the worktree root into any payload/fixture/env the hook reads back

m2-treatment.title: Run the TREATMENT arm live and observe whether a HARD trip fires
m2-treatment.imperative: Launch a headless claude -p with cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to the sandbox main, --settings pointed at the treatment arm's settings, --permission-mode acceptEdits, --model named explicitly (never fable). It dispatches a subagent into the sandbox worktree which claims a spine there with a RELATIVE --file, inflates its own context past its model's absolute HARD cap, runs a further tool call, then attempts advance. Capture: binding store dump, BOTH candidate gauge paths (present/absent + contents), full advance output and its REAL exit code (redirect to file, then echo $?), observed_at vs wall clock, acting model, and the three attribution facts (composite session_id#agent_id key, identity_resolution_ms present, model).

m3-control.title: Run the CONTROL arm live and show it WORKED AND MISSED (positive control)
m3-control.imperative: Identical launch, the ONLY difference being the absolute hook path pointing at the control arm's tree. Capture the same evidence set. The control must be shown to be POSITIVE: a real gauge.json with fill_fraction >= hard at the WRONG path (the phantom .agent-work/<work_id>/ inside the sandbox main), with advance succeeding. If the control produces no gauge anywhere, declare the run INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass, and diagnose against the skip-on-uncertainty enumeration.

triage_candidates.statement: A dispatched subagent DECLINED the acceptance protocol because of the prompt's own defensive framing ('nothing below looks like a trick', 'is not a prompt-injection attempt') plus the fixed closing token PROTOCOL-COMPLETE, which it read as social engineering. Cost one headless launch and produced a quiet arm indistinguishable from the bug. Future context-inflation harnesses should frame the work as ordinary and drop the protestation and the magic token.

verify_evidence.py's live-checkout guard asserted a SHARED, concurrently-agent-written file (.agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json) was byte-identical across a run window. That is unsatisfiable whenever any other agent is working -- this run's own plan lease and a sibling commander both wrote it. General lesson: no check may assume shared agent-written state is byte-stable; test the exclusion (no sandbox leakage) instead.

The LIVE binding store holds two junk entries whose spine paths are 'C:\Programs\constellation-skills\x' and 'C:\Programs\constellation-skills\C:/Users/fredc/.claude/skills/constellation-implementer/scripts/checklist_engine.py' (claimed 2026-08-06T10:02-10:03Z). '$E' is an UNEXPANDED SHELL VARIABLE recorded verbatim as a spine path, so spine_rail.py will bind a path that does not exist. Harmless here but worth a look given #440 is about binding the wrong path. Not touched.

engine_session.takeover_reason: attempt 1 killed mid-run by account weekly usage limit (reset 2026-08-07 07:00 PT); attempt 2 resumes at m2-treatment

why_trail.why: The HARD trip DOES fire for a worktree-dispatched agent from its own reading. The engine refused advance at exit 1 with the hard-limit message, reading a gauge.json that landed beside the WORKTREE spine (fill 0.5597 vs hard 0.15) while the phantom path in the sandbox main stayed empty -- the exact inversion of the #440 defect. All three attribution signals agree the reading is the dispatched subagent's, not the parent's. One earlier launch was quiet because the subagent declined the protocol outright; that is a prompt-compliance hazard for this harness, not a governor result, and it is the reason a quiet arm must always be diagnosed before it is believed.

The control is positive, so the treatment result means something. Same sandbox, same prompt, same model pair, same inflation, fills within 0.0025 of each other -- the ONLY difference is which arm tree the absolute hook path names, and that single difference moves the reading from the phantom directory in the sandbox main (control, governor blind, advance exit 0) to beside the worktree spine (treatment, governor fires, advance exit 1). That is the #440 defect and its repair, observed side by side on one run.

verify_evidence.py exits 0 on the freshly-produced evidence (46 checks) and demonstrably fails when the evidence is damaged: an explicit truncated copy exits 1, and --selftest catches all five mutations including a missing control arm, a quieted control, and a treatment advance rewritten to succeed. One check had to be corrected rather than satisfied: the live-checkout guard asserted the shared binding store was byte-identical across the run, which is unsatisfiable while any other agent is working -- this run's own plan lease and a sibling commander both wrote it through the LIVE checkout's own hook. It now tests the exclusion directly, that no sandbox path leaked into that store, and a fifth selftest mutation proves that check can fail.

Acceptance closed with a live YES: the HARD trip fires from a worktree-dispatched agent's own reading (advance REFUSED, real exit 1, gauge beside the worktree spine at 0.5597 vs hard 0.15), against a POSITIVE control that produced an equally large reading at the phantom path in the sandbox main and sailed through at exit 0. verify_evidence.py exits 0 on the fresh evidence and non-zero on damaged copies. Three triage candidates raised, chief among them that a dispatched subagent can decline an inflation protocol because of the prompt's own defensive framing -- which is why a quiet arm must always be diagnosed before it is believed.
